label: [ K-IG 교육 Reading 211 ]

blocks.text: When we think of the public face of scientific genius, we often remember someone with old and graying appearances. For example, we think of Albert Einstein's disheveled hair. Charles Darwin's majestic beard. Isaac Newton's wrinkled visage.

Yet the truth is that most of the scientific breakthroughs that have changed our lives are usually made by people who are still in their 30s--and that includes Einstein, Newton and Darwin. Indeed, not surprisingly, younger scientists are less affected by (the intellectual dogma of the day) than their elders.
They question authority instinctively. They do not believe it when they are told that a new idea is crazy, so they are free to do the impossible.

readingSentences.english: Scientific curiosity drives human progress beyond established boundaries.
readingSentences.korean: 과학적 호기심은 기존의 한계를 넘어 인류의 진보를 견인한다.

readingSentences.english: Researchers continually challenge old models in search of deeper truths.
readingSentences.korean: 연구자들은 더 깊은 진실을 찾아 끊임없이 낡은 이론 모델들에 도전한다.

readingSentences.english: A single breakthrough can revolutionize medicine, energy, or communications.
readingSentences.korean: 단 하나의 획기적인 발견이 의학이나 에너지, 통신 분야에 일대 혁명을 일으킬 수 있다.

readingSentences.english: Fostering rigorous research is an investment in global well-being.
readingSentences.korean: 엄밀한 기초 연구를 육성하는 것은 전 지구적 복지를 위한 필수적 투자이다.
